blocks.text: Zoning Guide for Langley, Surrey, Abbotsford & Delta
Zoning in Abbotsford, Langley, Surrey, Delta and the Fraser Valley

parts.t: Plain-English summaries of farm, rural, acreage and residential zones, with a link to the official bylaw for every zone. Start with the agricultural and rural zones if you are looking at a farm or acreage, or search any zone code.
Checked against each official bylaw on October 2, 2026. Zoning changes often, so always confirm with the municipality.

These summaries may not reflect recent amendments and are not legal advice. Always confirm zoning, permitted uses and ALR status with the municipality and the Agricultural Land Commission before you buy.

Type an address to see its zoning, ALR status, lot size and other public map checks. It covers Surrey, Langley (City and Township) and Abbotsford for now. Anywhere else, send me the address and I'll check its zoning, ALR status and what you can build before you write an offer.
General information from public municipal and provincial maps, not a survey or legal advice. The address is only used to look up public map data. Prefer to write directly?

blocks.text: RR7s Rural Residential 7 Secondary Dwelling Zone

parts.t: One duplex, or one single family dwelling with a secondary detached unit.
The Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) is provincial. On ALR land, Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) rules apply in addition to municipal zoning, and local governments can add further restrictions.
Generally one residence is allowed per parcel. The principal residence can be up to 500 m² in total floor area, with no more than 1,000 m² of fill placed for its construction.
A secondary suite is allowed only inside the principal residence, and only if local bylaws allow it.

One additional detached residence may be allowed without an ALC application if only one residence exists when construction starts: up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha. It does not need to be for farm help. Local zoning may still limit it.
Most subdivision of ALR land needs ALC approval, including parcels under 2 acres.
Source: Agricultural Land Commission, checked October 2, 2026.

blocks.text: Before you buy: what to check

parts.t: The zone and its minimum lot size.
Don't assume a property can be subdivided. Check the minimum lot size, and on ALR land, ALC approval.
Zoning and ALC rules both limit homes, suites and coach houses.
Ask for septic records and have the system inspected. Septic rules come from the health authority.
Find out whether it's a well or municipal water. For a well, ask about yield, water quality and any water licence.
Ask BC Assessment whether the property has farm class. If you plan to keep livestock or poultry, ask about BC's Premises ID program.
I'll check its zoning and ALR status and tell you what to confirm with the municipality. Or look it up yourself at the top of the page.

items.t: A1 zoning in BC: what it means for buyers
Guide to buying land in BC's ALR

parts.t: This directory is a general summary prepared from each municipality's published zoning bylaw and the Agricultural Land Commission's website, checked October 2, 2026. Bylaws are amended often, site-specific zones and covenants may apply, and summaries leave out many regulations (setbacks, density, parking, floodplain and development permit requirements, among others). It is not legal, planning or survey advice. Always confirm zoning, permitted uses, lot size and ALR status directly with the municipality and the ALC before you buy, sell or build. City of Langley and Pitt Meadows are not covered here.
Jared Gibbons, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty ·
